findings.evidence: a dying courier entrusts American girl Jane Finn with secret Allied papers as the Lusitania sinks — 'He took her hand. "Good-bye. Good luck to you"... Her hand closed on the oilskin packet'
cash-strapped Tuppence Cowley and Tommy Beresford launch 'The Young Adventurers, Ltd.' and hear rumors of Jane Finn — 'I passed two Johnnies to-day talking about some one called Jane Finn'
Mr. Whittington appears and Mr. Brown is identified as the criminal overlord who will kill to get the treaty — 'He is the master criminal of this age… Mr. Brown'

Tuppence infiltrates Mrs. Vandemeyer's household; Tommy traces Boris to a Soho hideout, is captured, and is aided by Annette — 'The door opened—not Conrad, but a girl with a tray… My name is Annette, monsieur'
Julius P. Hersheimmer claiming to be Jane's cousin, Sir James Peel Edgerton, and Mr. Carter explaining the treaty's stakes — 'I'm Jane's first cousin… Sir James Peel Edgerton… Mr. Carter'
radical agitators and foreign agents orchestrated by Mr. Brown, with Jane's amnesia masking the truth — 'Janet Vandemeyer is suffering from a complete loss of memory'
Mrs. Vandemeyer dies before she can confess — 'Mrs. Vandemeyer was dead—must have been dead for hours… Is it only chance?'
Tommy escapes, the trio follow leads to a nursing home and find Jane alive but memoryless — 'At Bournemouth nursing home… Janet Vandemeyer is suffering from a complete loss of memory'

Jane explains she hid the treaty behind a Marguerite picture in the Soho room — 'I unhooked one of the pictures—Marguerite with her casket of jewels… slipped the two stuck-together pages… between the canvas and the paper'
first recovery yields only 'With the compliments of Mr. Brown' — 'Across the sheet, in neat brown printing, ran the words: WITH THE COMPLIMENTS OF MR. BROWN'
fake telegram lures Tuppence into danger and the hunters race back to Soho — 'Come at once, Moat House… signed your name, and she fell into the trap like a lamb'
they find the real papers and Sir James reveals himself as Mr. Brown — 'Jane went straight to the picture of Marguerite… "I am Mr. Brown…"'

Tommy and Julius overpower Sir James, who kills himself with poison from his signet ring — 'His left hand—bearing the big signet ring—flashed to his lips… with a long convulsive shudder he crumpled to the floor. An odour of bitter almonds filled the air'

Brown dead, conspiracy collapses, general strike fizzles, Jane vindicated — 'The much-heralded Labour Day had passed like any other day… the reign of terror failed to materialize… Deprived of their chief, the organization fell to pieces'
Julius wins Jane's heart, Tommy and Tuppence confess their love and plan marriage — 'I love you now, Julius…
